title: Guwahati: Petroleum Dealers Defer Indefinite Strike After Talks with Oil Companies

ai.summary: The North East India Petroleum Dealers' Association (NEIPDA) deferred its proposed indefinite strike after talks with oil companies, aiming to address grievances like tank truck consortium arrangements, lubricant billing, and subsidy reimbursements without disrupting fuel supply.

facts.claim: NEIPDA deferred its proposed indefinite strike scheduled to begin at 6 am on November 23
facts.quote: The North East India Petroleum Dealers' Association (NEIPDA), Greater Guwahati Unit, has deferred its proposed indefinite strike scheduled to begin at 6 am on November 23 following discussions with senior officials of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL).

facts.claim: The oil marketing companies (OMCs) provided clarifications and assurances and agreed to take corrective measures on certain issues
facts.quote: The decision followed a meeting held on November 19 at the Indian Oil AOD State Office in Noonmati, where the association raised several longstanding grievances and operational difficulties faced by petroleum dealers. The oil marketing companies (OMCs) provided clarifications and assurances and agreed to take corrective measures on certain issues.

facts.claim: On the discontinuation of the existing tank truck consortium arrangement involving Maa Filling Station and Changsari Service Station, IOCL agreed to allow Maa Filling Station's tank truck to form a consortium with two new retail outlets - Omkar Filling Station and Biulina Servo Station - as an interim arrangement
facts.quote: On the discontinuation of the existing tank truck consortium arrangement involving Maa Filling Station and Changsari Service Station, IOCL agreed to allow Maa Filling Station's tank truck to form a consortium with two new retail outlets - Omkar Filling Station and Biulina Servo Station - as an interim arrangement.

facts.claim: IOCL also agreed to seek special approval to reinstate the consortium arrangement with Changsari Service Station within 30 days
facts.quote: IOCL also agreed to seek special approval to reinstate the consortium arrangement with Changsari Service Station within 30 days.

facts.claim: HPCL assured that cases involving advance billing without timely delivery would be examined and resolved
facts.quote: HPCL assured that cases involving advance billing without timely delivery would be examined and resolved.

facts.claim: BPCL clarified that it did not process bills unless demand was generated by the respective retail outlets
facts.quote: BPCL clarified that it did not process bills unless demand was generated by the respective retail outlets, while IOCL said lubricant billing should be based on actual demand.

facts.claim: On delays in reimbursement of subsidies and Weights and Measures calibration charges, IOCL attributed a temporary disruption in processing claims to the migration of its online portal in March-April 2026
facts.quote: On delays in reimbursement of subsidies and Weights and Measures calibration charges, IOCL attributed a temporary disruption in processing claims to the migration of its online portal in March-April 2026.

facts.claim: IOCL assured the association that any outstanding claims identified would be coordinated with dealers and field officers and cleared within two to three days
facts.quote: It assured the association that any outstanding claims identified would be coordinated with dealers and field officers and cleared within two to three days.

facts.claim: The association also complained about alleged high-handedness and unprofessional conduct by certain field officers
facts.quote: The association also complained about alleged high-handedness and unprofessional conduct by certain field officers.

facts.claim: All three OMCs assured that complaints could be brought to the attention of senior officials at their divisional and state offices for appropriate intervention
facts.quote: All three OMCs assured that complaints could be brought to the attention of senior officials at their divisional and state offices for appropriate intervention.

facts.claim: IOCL separately clarified the adjustment of a Rs 25 lakh security deposit made twice by Maa Filling Station
facts.quote: IOCL separately clarified the adjustment of a Rs 25 lakh security deposit made twice by Maa Filling Station.

facts.claim: Regarding the proposed transportation tender for Betkuchi Terminal, IOCL said it would be exclusively for bottom-loading tank trucks
facts.quote: Regarding the proposed transportation tender for Betkuchi Terminal, IOCL said it would be exclusively for bottom-loading tank trucks.

facts.claim: The new tank lorry filling facility, equipped with bottom-loading infrastructure, was under construction and expected to be commissioned by March 2027
facts.quote: The new tank lorry filling facility, equipped with bottom-loading infrastructure, was under construction and expected to be commissioned by March 2027.

facts.claim: The conversion of existing tank trucks from top-loading to bottom-loading would be phased, with both facilities operating initially to avoid disruption to transportation and supply arrangements
facts.quote: The conversion of existing tank trucks from top-loading to bottom-loading would be phased, with both facilities operating initially to avoid disruption to transportation and supply arrangements.

facts.claim: NEIPDA's Greater Guwahati Unit president Rajib Goswami and general secretary Arup Goswami said the strike had been deferred in the interest of uninterrupted public supply of petroleum products and to allow the grievances to be addressed through dialogue
facts.quote: In a statement, NEIPDA's Greater Guwahati Unit president Rajib Goswami and general secretary Arup Goswami said the strike had been deferred in the interest of uninterrupted public supply of petroleum products and to allow the grievances to be addressed through dialogue.

ai.background_note: The North East India Petroleum Dealers' Association (NEIPDA) deferred its strike after negotiations with major oil companies to address operational grievances without disrupting fuel supply.
